S15.01.note: The name on the button is data-driven (selectedModel.name); the Code line's quoted line 1324 moved, but the button is rendered from triggerLabel at ComposerFooter.tsx:1460-1483.
steps: Sign in and open New chat.
Look at the model button in the composer footer and note the model name shown.
Click the model button and pick a different model in the list.
Send a short message and compare the name on the composer footer with the Expected text: the composer still shows the model the next message uses.
S15.01.where: New chat > composer footer model button. The button shows the name of the selected model, with "Change model" as its accessible name.

S15.02.note: The developer name comes from catalogue data (entry.developerLabel), so the exact names are not in the code. The full catalogue list is reached through the picker; its opening control was not traced.
steps: Open New chat and click the model button in the composer footer.
In the list, read the small grey line under each model name and look at the provider logo.
Compare with Expected: each model shows which company makes it.
S15.02.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model list. Each row shows a provider logo and a developer name line.

S15.03.note: The Family value is data-driven. I did not confirm the visible group heading text used for grouping, only that groupByModelLine builds the groups.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Click the help icon (accessible name "About <model name>") on a model row.
Read the Family line on the card.
Go back with "Back to the model list" and check that models of the same family sit together in the list, as Expected says.
S15.03.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model list > "About" button on a model row (accessible name "About <model name>") > Family line.

steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Click the search field labelled "Search models".
Type part of a model name, such as qwen.
Compare: the list narrows to matching models.
S15.04.where: New chat > composer footer model button > search field labelled "Search models".

steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Click the star button on a model row (accessible name "Add <model name> to favourites").
Close the list and open it again.
Compare: the starred model appears in the "Favourites" section at the top.
S15.05.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model list > star button (accessible name "Add <model name> to favourites"). Favourites appear under the "Favourites" heading.

S15.06.note: The Recent rail is in the model list; its exact position relative to the short list was not traced.
steps: Use two or three different models in a few chats.
Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Click the "Recent" rail.
Compare: the models you used most recently are listed.
S15.06.where: New chat > composer footer model button > "Recent" rail in the model list.

steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look at the section titled "Recommended".
Compare: it shows a short list of recommended models for your plan.
S15.07.where: New chat > composer footer model button > "Recommended" section at the top of the list.

labels.text: Picks the best model for each message

S15.08.note: The auto row label is built from data (shortList.auto.label); I used the fixed guidance text as the visible words.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Click the first row, the Auto row.
Send a message and check the model name on the composer footer and the model that answers.
Compare: Auto picks a model for each message, as Expected says.
S15.08.where: New chat > composer footer model button > first row "Auto" in the list (guidance text "Picks the best model for each message").

S15.09.needs: a paid account for models outside the Free plan
S15.09.note: Outside the requested range; included for reference only.
steps: Open Settings and go to General.
Find the "Default model" select (its first option is "Last used").
Choose a model, then open a new chat.
Compare: the new chat starts with the model you chose.
Click the model button in the composer footer.
Click a model row that is not locked.
Type a message and send it.
Compare: the answer comes from the model you picked, and the composer shows that model name.
S15.10.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row.

S15.11.note: The guidance text is data-driven. When no guidance exists the row falls back to the provider name, so some rows may show only the provider.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Read the short grey line under each model name.
Click the help icon "About <model name>" and read the card.
Compare: each model has a short line about what it is good for.
S15.11.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row guidance line under the model name. Full card: "About <model name>" button.

steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look at the small chips on a model row, or open its "About" card.
Find the "Vision" chip on a model that accepts images.
Compare: the chip shows which inputs the model accepts.
S15.12.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row or "About <model name>" card > capability chips.

S15.13.note: Whether a model shows an output chip depends on catalogue data.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look for chips such as "Image out", "Video out" or "Audio out".
Compare the chips with the outputs the model produces.
S15.13.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row or "About <model name>" card > capability chips.

steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Find the "Tools" chip on a model row.
Open the "About" card for a model with and without the chip.
Compare: the chip appears only on models that can use tools.
S15.14.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row or "About <model name>" card > capability chips.

S15.15.note: The figures appear only on the About card, and are left out when the catalogue has no value. Not on the row itself.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Click the help icon "About <model name>" on a model row.
Read the "Context ceiling" and "Output ceiling" lines.
Compare: they show the context size in K or M.
S15.15.where: New chat > composer footer model button > "About <model name>" button > "Context ceiling" line.

S15.16.note: No relative speed label found. Searched for speed, faster, slower and latency in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/modelPicker.ts, packages/ai/routing/src/model-picker.ts, ModelCatalogue.tsx and ComposerFooter.tsx. The only match is the Fast mode text "Faster answers at ... the usage" (ComposerFooter.tsx:2034), which is not a speed comparison between models.

S15.17.note: Free-pool models show no credit figures. The bar text is generated from data.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look at the price bars on each row, or hover a bar to see its title.
Click the help icon "About <model name>" and read "Credits per 1M tokens" and "Typical message".
Compare: more filled bars or larger numbers mean a higher cost or faster use of the allowance.
S15.17.where: New chat > composer footer model button > price bars on a model row (accessible text "Price band X of Y") and the "About <model name>" card > "Credits per 1M tokens" and "Typical message".

S15.18.note: The plan name comes from resolvePlanLockLabel (packages/ai/routing/src/model-picker.ts:247); the fallback text is "Upgrade".
steps: Sign in with a Free account.
Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Find a row with an "Upgrade" label, marked with a lock.
Compare: the row names the plan that unlocks the model, as Expected says.
S15.18.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row marked "Upgrade" (locked rows show the plan that unlocks them).

S15.19.needs: a preview or experimental model in the catalogue
S15.19.note: I did not confirm that any preview model is in the current catalogue, so the badge may not be visible.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look for a badge reading "Preview", "Experimental", "Beta" or "Alpha" on a row.
Compare: the model carries the badge, as Expected says.
S15.19.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row badge (Preview, Experimental, Beta or Alpha).

S15.20.needs: a model with a retirement date in the catalogue
S15.20.note: The date comes from catalogue data; I did not confirm that a model with a retirement date exists now.
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look for a row whose grey line reads "Leaving" followed by a date.
Compare: the notice shows the retirement date before the model leaves the list.
S15.20.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row guidance reads "Leaving <date>".

S15.21.needs: a provider in a degraded state, which a tester cannot set up
S15.21.note: The state depends on live provider availability; the row text is "Temporarily unavailable" inside the catalogue (ModelCatalogue.tsx:41).
steps: Open the model list from the composer footer model button.
Look for a row whose grey line reads "Unavailable right now".
Click that row and check that the model is not selected.
Compare: the row is marked unavailable and cannot be picked.
S15.21.where: New chat > composer footer model button > model row guidance reads "Unavailable right now" and the row cannot be picked.

S15.22.needs: a reasoning model, and a paid account for the higher levels
S15.22.note: The control is shown only for models with an effort ladder; Settings > General also has the same label.
steps: Select a reasoning model in the composer footer model button.
Click the "Reasoning effort" control in the composer footer.
Drag the slider to a different level, or pick an option.
Send a message and compare the level chosen with Expected: the model thinks at that level.
S15.22.where: New chat > composer footer reasoning control (the control whose accessible name starts "Reasoning effort:") > effort slider labelled "Reasoning effort". Settings > General > "Reasoning effort".

S15.23.needs: a paid account and a model with a fast tier
S15.23.note: The switch is disabled when fast mode is not allowed for the account or workspace; the enclosing popover was inferred from file order and not run.
steps: Select a model that offers a faster tier in the composer footer model button.
Click the composer footer reasoning control.
Turn on the "Fast mode" switch.
Send a message and check the "Fast" pill and the usage note: faster answers at the stated usage multiplier.
S15.23.where: New chat > composer footer reasoning control > "Fast mode" switch. The "Fast" pill appears when it is on.

S15.24.note: The Settings entry point to Settings > Personalization was not traced.
steps: Click the "Style" button in the composer footer.
Find the "Response Length" row.
Click "Brief" or "Thorough".
Send the same question twice, once with each setting, and compare the answer lengths with Expected.
S15.24.where: New chat > composer footer "Style" button > "Response Length" row (Brief, Default, Thorough). Also Settings > Personalization > "Response length".

S15.29.note: The choice is saved in localStorage under the key agi-model-store (apps/web/shared/stores/model-store.ts:376); it is per browser, not per account.
steps: Choose a model in the composer footer model button.
Close the browser tab and open the app again.
Open New chat and read the model name on the composer footer.
Compare with Expected: the chosen model is still selected. If Settings > General > "Default model" is set to a fixed model, that setting wins over this memory.
S15.29.where: No control. Effect is seen after a restart: the composer model name in a new chat matches the model last chosen.

S15.30.needs: an account with more than one model available
S15.30.note: The per-conversation save path is handleConversationModelChange in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; the only visible error is the toast 'Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.' Default-versus-conversation behaviour in a new chat was not traced in code.
steps: Open or start a conversation in the web app.
Click the model name button at the bottom of the message box (it opens the picker titled Models).
Choose a different model from the list.
Send a message in this same conversation and wait for the answer.
Open a new chat and look at the model name in its composer.
Compare: this conversation keeps the model you chose, and the new chat shows the default model.
S15.30.where: Composer footer > model name button > Models (pick a model), then send a message in the same conversation

S15.31.needs: an account with more than one model available
S15.31.note: The refresh icon has no visible text, only an aria-label 'Regenerate response'. The model list comes from regenerateModelOptions, and the override is passed in handleRegenerateMessage in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.
steps: Send a message and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover under the answer and click the refresh icon (it opens a menu).
Under Try again with, click a model name.
Look at the new answer, and then open the composer model picker.
Compare: the new answer comes from the model you picked, and the composer still shows the conversation's previous model.
S15.31.where: Under an answer, click the refresh icon (Regenerate response) > Try again with > pick a model

S15.32.note: The label text is built at runtime from the model id (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx around line 2411), so no fixed visible words exist to quote. It is hidden until hover on pointer devices.
steps: Send a message and wait for the answer to finish.
Move the mouse over the answer (on touch screens the label is always shown).
Read the small muted model name under the answer.
Compare: the name matches the model that actually answered, shown on the composer or in the Try again with menu.
S15.32.where: Hover over an answer; the model name that answered shows under it (data-testid message-answered-by in MessageBubble)

S15.33.needs: none; a model failure or outage is needed to trigger the notice, which a tester cannot force from the UI
S15.33.note: The notice text is generated at runtime by describeFallbackReason (packages/contracts/types/src/chat-fallback-reason.ts; apps/web/lib/chat-fallback-reason.ts). The close control's aria-label is 'Dismiss model substitution notice' but it has no visible text. The notice is not shown while the answer is still streaming.
steps: Send a message with a model; wait for the answer to finish.
Look under the answer for a small notice with an alert icon and a close control.
Read the notice text: it says the different model answered and gives the reason.
Click the close control to dismiss the notice.
Compare: the notice names the model that answered and the reason, and it appears only when the chosen model failed or was unavailable.
S15.33.where: A notice appears under an answer when a fallback happened (role status, data-testid fallback-reason-notice)

S15.34.needs: a file or image to upload, and an account with a model that cannot read it
S15.34.note: The warning sentences come from evaluateModelCompatibility at runtime; the Keep button text is built from the current model name, so it is not quoted as a fixed label.
steps: Attach an image to the chat (use the attach control in the message box).
Click the model name button and open the Models picker.
Choose a model that cannot read images or other files in this chat.
Look for the line Switch to <model name>? with a warning sentence under it.
Read the sentence, then compare: it says what will be lost, and the two buttons are Switch anyway and Keep <current model name>.
S15.34.where: Composer footer > model name button > Models > choose a model that cannot handle the current chat

S15.35.needs: a file or image to upload; a Free account shows Use Free Auto instead of Use Auto
S15.35.note: The alert text is chosen at runtime by attachmentConflictKind. For local-model attachments the alert shows Switch to a cloud model and Remove attachments instead (ChatComposerNew.tsx around line 5321-5357).
steps: Attach an image or document to the chat.
Click the model name button and choose a model that cannot read that file type.
Look at the alert above the message box: it says the selected model can't read the attachment.
To keep the files, click Use Auto, or click Choose a compatible model and pick a listed model.
To drop them instead, click Remove attachments.
Compare: the files are kept with a model that can read them, or removed, and the alert goes away.
S15.35.where: Attach a file or image, then choose a model that cannot read it; an alert appears above the message box with Use Auto, Remove attachments and Choose a compatible model
